html:
Ghana is a country on the Gulf of Guinea in West Africa, independent since 1957. The map uses the name twice: from 800 to 1200 for the medieval Ghana Empire far to the north-west, in the Sahel, and from 1920 for the modern state.

The two are not the same place. When the British Gold Coast colony became independent, its leaders took the name of the old empire as a symbol of African greatness, even though the empire had lain hundreds of kilometres away in what is now Mauritania and Mali.

The modern country's own past:

  • The forest was the land of the Akan peoples, who mined and traded gold for centuries.
  • From 1482 the Portuguese, then the Dutch, British and others built forts on the coast, starting with Elmina, to trade gold and later enslaved people.
  • In the 1700s and 1800s the Asante kingdom dominated the interior until Britain conquered it in 1900 and 1901.
  • Cocoa, brought in by Tetteh Quarshie in 1879, made the colony the world's leading grower.

Under Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana was the first colony in sub-Saharan Africa to win independence, on 6 March 1957, and its example spread across the continent. Nkrumah built the Akosombo Dam and pushed for African unity, but grew authoritarian and was overthrown in 1966. Years of coups followed, many led by Jerry Rawlings, until a return to multi-party elections in 1992. Since then power has changed hands peacefully several times, and gold, cocoa and, from 2010, oil drive the economy.
sum: Ghana is a country on the Gulf of Guinea in West Africa, independent since 1957. The map uses the name twice: from 800 to 1200 for the medieval Ghana Empire far to the north-west, in the Sahel, and from 1920 for the modern state.
